laneFindings.title: pdf-lib THROWS on a /MaxLen overflow and the shared finalizer does not catch it
laneFindings.what: A text widget may declare /MaxLen. A value longer than it raises ExceededMaxLengthError, which nothing catches, so the build DIES rather than reporting a value that did not fit.
laneFindings.foundOn: id_clean_slate_shield-set: five of the Idaho shielding petition's thirteen widgets declare /MaxLen (35, 35, 35, 16 and 30) and the corpus's standard boundary participant exceeds all five. The build wrote the canonical fixture and then crashed on the boundary one.
laneFindings.whatThisLaneDid: Did NOT repair it — rcap-text-fitting.mjs is outside this lane's owned paths and every family shares it. Instead each build script in this lane asks the same question with the same binder BEFORE calling the finalizer, and refuses an over-length value by role, per fixture. Backporting the guard to the two Arkansas families left all eight of their fixture PDFs byte-identical.
laneFindings.whoShouldOwnIt: a repair lane with rcap-official-forms in scope
laneFindings.severity: A family with a /MaxLen widget and a long fixture value cannot be built at all until either the finalizer catches this or each builder guards it.

laneFindings.title: rowIndexOf reads any trailing digit as a charge-row index, including a page suffix
laneFindings.what: A field named for its page or its position — Court Case Number_2, OFFENSE 3, CauseNumber1 — is read as row 1, 2 or 0 of a repeating charge table. Where the caller supplies that many charges the blank does not stay empty: it receives a DIFFERENT charge's value.
foundOn: ar-act531-set: OFFENSE 3 is paragraph 2's 'convicted of the offense(s) of' line, and the boundary fixture drew 'Driving while license suspended' onto the conviction line of a petition about a controlled-substance offence.
the Alabama C-94A: the page 2 and page 3 Court Case Number headers would carry a different charge's case number.
the Indiana CCA bundle: CauseNumber1 wrote this matter's cause number into the Appearance's RELATED CASES table, so the filing would state that the case is related to itself.
laneFindings.whatThisLaneDid: Refused every affected field by role and recorded why. On the Alabama family the two page headers are declared required-before-filing for a fact the platform HOLDS, and that declaration is listed in declaredRequiredBeforeFilingWithHeldFact on the field map so it is weighed rather than discovered.
laneFindings.whoShouldOwnIt: a repair lane with rcap-official-forms in scope

laneFindings.title: Widget names are shifted by one on four of this lane's forms, and the shift is not always harmless
laneFindings.what: On the AR Act 531 pair, the AR CS-possession pair, the Idaho shielding petition and the Alabama C-94A, caption widgets are named after text that is not beside them. Three of the four produce a WRONG WRITE rather than an empty blank: Idaho would print the participant's state as a judicial district, Alabama would print the petitioner's own city, ZIP and telephone as the licensing board's service address, and Arkansas would leave the county unreachable.
laneFindings.whatThisLaneDid: Introduced a narrow printed-label correction mechanism: it replaces the harvested caption of ONE named widget with the printed text read at that widget's own measured position, and records the correction, the value it replaced and the measured evidence on the field-map row. Used only for identity, contact and venue facts, never to reach an offence, charge or statute blank.
laneFindings.aCautionForWhoeverReusesIt: A correction can itself cause a wrong write. On the Indiana bundle a correction reading "Petitioner's fax number" made the binder match its full-name descriptor on the word Petitioner and draw the participant's name into the fax box. The name-placement allowlist caught it and failed the build; the word came out of the label. Any lane adopting this mechanism should keep that guard on.
